mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 rally over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from a flat market.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which compresses wage growth and increases input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit growth expectations deteriorate.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from a positive threshold of +0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding decline in unemployment, signals supply-side disruptions that raise inflationary pressures and depress equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months AND UNRATE monthly change >= -0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 3% signals an emergency easing, which immediately boosts risk appetite and triggers a positive S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >1% in one month to below 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a precautionary savings surge, which typically precedes a decline in consumer discretionary equities over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous 3-month average AND GDPC1 monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deepening labor market weakness, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings pressure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month signals a classic positive supply shock, which typically precedes a short-lived positive S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days before profit margin concerns dominate.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.5% AND UNRATE monthly change < -0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.
